name: Trust Wallet Wallet
rootCause: The Trust Wallet browser extension suffered a software supply chain attack when attackers — as part of a broader npm-level campaign dubbed Shai-Hulud — compromised Trust Wallet's Chrome Web Store API key weeks before the incident. Using that key, they bypassed the standard internal release process and published a malicious version 2.68 directly to the Chrome Web Store on December 24, 2025. The rogue extension contained a bundled JavaScript file (4482.js) that, upon wallet unlock, captured the user's mnemonic phrase or private key via the GET_SEED_PHRASE call and silently exfiltrated it to an attacker-controlled server at api.metrics-trustwallet[.]com. Approximately $8.5 million was drained from 2,520 wallet addresses in Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana before Trust Wallet pulled the extension and replaced it with a clean v2.69. Trust Wallet has issued an official notice confirming that version 2.68 of its browser extension contains a security vulnerability, and advised all users running version 2.68 to immediately disable it and upgrade to version 2.69. According to SlowMist’s analysis, this backdoor incident originated from a malicious modification of Trust Wallet’s internal codebase (analytics service logic), rather than the introduction of a compromised third-party package (e.g., a malicious npm package). Between December 24 and 26, 2025, a malicious update to the Trust Wallet browser extension enabled a supply chain compromise, letting an attacker steal user seeds and drain $8.5 million from wallets across Ethereum, Bitcoin, and Solana. Recovery and verification for reimbursement remain ongoing, with transaction-level details undisclosed. The attacker obtained Trust Wallet’s Chrome Web Store publishing API key and browser extension source after developer GitHub secrets were exposed in the Sha1-Hulud npm supply chain incident.
